card.title: BBB SMA
card.body: An actively managed, investment-grade credit strategy of senior and subordinated notes issued by banks and A-grade insurers.

hero.title: BBB SMA
hero.subtitle: An actively managed, investment-grade credit strategy of bank and insurer notes.

statement.title: How the portfolio earns its return.
points: Every note pays a margin over BBSW and resets quarterly. Income moves with the cash rate rather than being locked in at purchase, and interest-rate risk stays negligible.
The return above cash comes from issue margins on bank and insurer paper — senior notes for stability, subordinated notes for incremental yield, all within investment grade.
The team sets the book line by line rather than tracking an index, and holds cash when credit does not pay for its risk.

about.title: About the strategy
about.body: An actively managed separately managed account of senior and subordinated floating-rate notes issued by major banks and A-grade insurers — twelve lines across nine issuers, run with the same discipline as the Arculus public funds.

atAGlance.title: At a glance
atAGlance.note: Terms are indicative and confirmed in mandate documentation.

processRiskControls.title: Process & risk controls
items: Active, fundamentals-driven analysis of bank and insurer issuers, favouring names with strong capital positions and stable ratings trajectories.
No single issuer exceeds 20% of the portfolio and no single line exceeds 11%, diversified across nine issuers.
The floating-rate structure limits interest-rate duration; the team rotates between senior and subordinated tranches as relative value shifts.
Positions, marks and cash are reconciled daily against trade, bond and cash-rate data feeds.

keyRisks.title: Key risks
paragraphs: Issuer default or downgrade can reduce income and capital value, and subordinated holdings rank behind senior creditors in a wind-up. Despite diversification limits, the portfolio holds a relatively small number of issuers, concentrated in banking and insurance.

Subordinated paper and smaller issuer lines may trade less liquidly in stressed markets, and credit spreads can still widen even where duration risk is limited. This is not a capital-guaranteed investment, and past performance is not indicative of future returns.
